title: server-audit.sh JSON report
description: The file that server-audit.sh --json FILE writes. Every field is described in docs/json-output.md.
$comment: schema_version 1. Adding a field, a check id or a category keeps schema_version: this schema allows extra fields and does not list the check ids. Removing or renaming a field, a check id or a status, or changing a field's type, bumps schema_version here (const) and in the JSON writer of server-audit.sh.

version.description: The audit's own version (AUDIT_VERSION in server-audit.sh), not server-prep's.

schema_version.description: The version of this format. It changes only when a change breaks the programs that read the file.

public_ip.description: The public IPv4 address from api.ipify.org, skipped with --no-network or without curl, or unknown when the lookup fails.

date.description: When the audit started (date -Is): ISO 8601 with the time zone offset.

root.description: true when the audit ran as root. false means partial results.

score.description: (pass*100 + warn*50) / (pass + warn + fail), rounded down; 0 when no check has PASS, WARN or FAIL.

summary.description: How many checks have each status.

fail.description: Checks with status FAIL. The audit exits 1 when it is not 0.

info.description: Checks with status INFO. They never count in the score.

checks.description: Every check that ran, in run order. An id can appear twice (panel.data_dir).

id.description: A stable id, <prefix>.<name>. docs/json-output.md lists every id.

category.description: The section the check belongs to: system, updates, ssh, firewall, ips, accounts, kernel, monitoring, services, resources, docker or panel. New sections can be added.

status.description: PASS, WARN (half a point), FAIL (the audit exits 1) or INFO (not scored).

title.description: The check's name, for people. It can change: match on id.

message.description: What the check found, for people. It can change: match on id and status.

fix.description: What to do, or an empty string when there is no fix.
